# 🧠 This week in Maia: Knowledge graph documents and rule visibility

MaiaNew Features

✨ This week, we're focused on giving you more visibility and more context. We've made Maia Team rules files transparent, so you can see exactly which rules are reaching Maia Team, and we've opened up the Context Engine to documents and unstructured data. For a full list of recent changes, be sure to check our \[changelog updates\]( [https://docs.maia.ai/docs/changelog](https://docs.maia.ai/docs/changelog)).

* * *

## **🔍 Maia Team rules files now show you what Maia Team can read**

When you edit Maia Team rules files in Designer, you can now see at a glance which rules are reaching Maia Team, and fix the rest in one click.

When you open a rules file in the Markdown editor, a new toolbar shows the file's size against the 12,000-character \[rules limit\]( [https://docs.maia.ai/docs/guides/maia-context-files#formatting-and-storing-context-files](https://docs.maia.ai/docs/guides/maia-context-files#formatting-and-storing-context-files)) and marks it as Loaded, Partially loaded, or Not loaded. Select the status to open a breakdown of every rules file on the branch. If any files don't fit, a **Fix with Maia** button asks Maia Team to bring them back under the limit.

This matters because all rules files are combined into one shared 12,000-character context, and files are filled in order. Even a small file can be left out if earlier files have already used up the space. Now you can see whether a rules file reaches Maia Team while you edit it.

**What's new:**

\- **Live status**: The status updates when you save, so you know immediately when you've gone over the limit or come back under it.

\- **Rules files only**: The information appears only in rules files, and the details open only when you ask for them, so other Markdown files work exactly as before.

\- **Fix with Maia**: Maia Team sees the size and load order of every file, then proposes a plan and waits for your approval before changing anything. It's available in three places: the editor toolbar, the branch-wide details view, and the Maia Team chat.

For more information about rules and context files, read \[Context files\]( [https://docs.maia.ai/docs/guides/maia-context-files](https://docs.maia.ai/docs/guides/maia-context-files)).

* * *

## **📚 Context Engine: Add documents and unstructured data to a knowledge graph**

You can now upload documents to a knowledge graph directly from the Context Engine UI, so your graph holds the written knowledge of your business, not only your warehouse and its pipelines.

**Why is this helpful?**

Much of your business logic lives in specifications, data dictionaries, runbooks, and policy documents. With document ingestion, Maia Team can use this knowledge to answer questions such as "what does this metric mean?" and "what is the rule for this field?" using your own documents.

**What's new:**

\- **Document ingestion**: In a graph, open \[\*\*Documents\*\*\]( [https://docs.maia.ai/docs/guides/managing-knowledge-graphs#documents](https://docs.maia.ai/docs/guides/managing-knowledge-graphs#documents)) and upload your files. Supported formats are PDF, Word (.docx), PowerPoint (.pptx), text, CSV, Markdown, HTML, and JSON.

\- **Linked into the graph**: The content of each document becomes nodes in the graph, alongside your warehouse and pipeline metadata, so Maia Team can use them together.

\- **Access controls**: These work the same way as for warehouse crawlers. Only people with access to the graph can see the content of the documents.

\- **Secure storage**: Document content is protected using envelope encryption.

**Rollout**

We're starting with the following limits to make sure every document produces a high-quality graph:

\- Up to 2 MB for each file.

\- Up to five ingestions running at the same time for each account.

We'll raise these limits as more kinds of documents are validated.

**How do I use it?**

1\. Open Context Engine from the hub and pick a knowledge graph, or create one.

2\. Go to **Documents** and choose **Upload documents**.

3\. Select your files and start the ingestion.

4\. When it finishes, ask Maia Team.
